question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: A NODE is a map whose entry t is text. Its display is chosen by t compared exactly (case-sensitive, whole text) against TABLE NODE; entries other than t and the field the row names (v or msg) are ignored (cu, bits, any extra key).
A none at a node position — tv itself, an element of a list or tuple, the second item of a record entry, or either item of a map entry — throws. CITED FIDELITY package

Anything else that is not a node — text, a number, a bool, a list, a map without a text t — displays "?". A node whose t names no row of TABLE NODE (an unknown tag, a differently cased tag) also displays "?".
none        | "null"
"undefined" | "undefined" (the js extension's present-but-valueless tag)
text        | v text -> QUOTE(v) (R4); v bool -> "true" / "false"; v none -> "null"; v absent -> ABSENT-MISSING (R5)
f64 i64 u64 bytes | v text -> v verbatim, never re-rendered (the f64 bits are not read); v none -> ABSENT-NULL; v absent -> ABSENT-MISSING
bigint      | v text -> v followed by "n" (v is not checked: "12" -> "12n", "" -> "n"); v true / false -> "truen" / "falsen"; v none -> "nulln"; v absent -> "undefinedn" (never ABSENT)
bool        | v true -> "true"; v false -> "false"; v text -> v verbatim; v none -> "null"; v absent -> "undefined"
throw       | "throw(" X ")" — X = QUOTE(msg) for a text msg; "true" / "false" for a bool msg; QUOTE of the empty text (two double quotes) when msg is none or absent
list tuple  | "[" the displays of the elements of v, joined by "," "]"
record      | "{" for each entry: FIELDNAME of its first item (R11), ":", the display of its second item; entries joined by ", " (comma, space) "}"
map         | "{" for each entry: the display of its first item, ":", the display of its second item; entries joined by "," "}"

QUOTE(s) = a double quote, s with each character replaced per TABLE ESCAPE, a double quote. Every character not in the table is written as itself — including "/", DEL (U+007F), U+0085, U+2028, U+2029 and every non-ASCII scalar. CITED FIDELITY package — the host's JSON string serializer
U+0022 quotation mark | "\""
U+005C reverse solidus | "\\"
any other U+0000..U+001F | "\u" then 4 LOWERCASE hex digits (U+001F -> "\u001f")

ABSENT. A text node with no v, and an f64/i64/u64/bytes node with no v or a none v, display no text: ABSENT-MISSING (no v) or ABSENT-NULL (v none). Where an ABSENT lands decides what it prints: as tv itself -> the result is none (both kinds); as an element of a list or tuple -> it contributes the empty text between its commas (both kinds: "[" ABSENT "]" is "[]", two ABSENTs are "[,]"); as a record entry's second item, or as either item of a map entry -> ABSENT-MISSING prints "undefined", ABSENT-NULL prints "null". CITED FIDELITY package

ENTRIES (record and map). Each element of v is an entry. A list entry supplies its first two items; items beyond the second are ignored. A text entry is read as the list of its Unicode scalar values: its first two items are one-character texts — a record writes the first as its field name through FIELDNAME (R11); every item that is DISPLAYED (a record's second, both of a map's) is a text, so "?" by R3. An entry with fewer than two items throws; an entry that is a none, bool, number or map throws. CITED FIDELITY package
The v of a list, tuple, record or map node must be a list: absent, none, text, bool, number or map -> throws.
Order is as stored: elements and entries print in the order v holds them — never sorted, never de-duplicated (a map with two equal keys prints both).
No escaping outside QUOTE: the verbatim v of the f64/i64/u64/bytes, bigint and bool rows of TABLE NODE is written raw, so a v holding ",", "]" or a quote is indistinguishable from structure.
Depth: the display has no nesting cap of its own; every depth the codec admits renders. CITED FIDELITY package
FIELDNAME(n) = n written as itself when n is a PLAIN IDENTIFIER, else QUOTE(n) (R4). CITED FIDELITY package — FINDINGS #95
